'''Lennart Eugén Eberson''' (5 January 1933 &ndash; 1 February 2000) was a [[Swedes|Swedish]] [[chemist]].

Eberson graduated with a Ph.D. degree in 1959 from [[Lund University]] with a thesis entitled "Studies in the Succinic and Glutaric Acid Series".<ref>{{cite book
|last=Eberson
|first=Lennart
|title=Studies in the Succinic and Glutaric Acid Series
|year=1959
|publisher=Esselte
|location=Stockholm
|language=en}}</ref>
<ref>{{cite journal
|last=Eberson
|first=Lennart
|title=Studies in the Succinic and Glutaric Acid Series
|journal=Svensk Kemisk Tidskrift
|year=1959
|volume=71
|pages=153
}}</ref>
From 1979 until his retirement in 1998, he was Professor of organic chemistry at Lund University. He authored several books, including the text books ''Introduktion till den organiska kemin'' (1965)<ref>{{cite book
|last=Eberson
|first=Lennart
|title=Introduktion till den organiska kemin
|year=1965
|publisher=Natur och Kultur
|location=Stockholm
|language=Swedish}}</ref>
and ''Organisk kemi'' (1970; 2nd edition 1977).<ref>{{cite book
|last=Eberson
|first=Lennart
|title=Organisk kemi
|edition=2nd
|year=1977
|publisher=AWE/Geber
|location=Stockholm
|language=Swedish}}</ref>
He was elected to the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences]] in 1974, and to the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] in 1988.

== Family ==
Lennart Eberson was son of shop manager Ebbe Eberson and Margit Eberson, née Fardrup. Married in 1957 to Anne-Marie Hansson, daughter of accountant Hilding Hansson and Margareta Hansson, née Lundgren.
